neboArmory.label: Armory
neboArmory.note: Brindle makes it light. Everything on Nebo has to be carried up something eventually.
neboArmory.name: Nebo Armory

neboCastlePath.label: Castle Path
neboCastlePath.note: The stream runs the width of the path. Follow it and it goes east — the way everything on this planet goes.
neboCastlePath.intro: The stream runs the width of the path. Follow it and it goes east — the way everything on this planet goes.
neboCastlePath.name: Nebo Castle Path

neboCommunityGarden.label: Community Garden
neboCommunityGarden.note: Five of them are up on the boards in cornhusk and leaf, and Marigold is waiting on somebody to call the play.
neboCommunityGarden.intro: Five of them are up on the boards in cornhusk and leaf, and Marigold is waiting on somebody to call the play.
neboCommunityGarden.name: Nebo Community Garden

neboDeepWoods.label: Deep Woods
neboDeepWoods.note: The trail is wider than the map says it is, and somebody has been cutting on both sides of it. There is smoke off the north-east spur, and it is somebody else’s smoke.
neboDeepWoods.intro: The trail is wider than the map says it is, and somebody has been cutting on both sides of it. There is smoke off the north-east spur, and it is somebody else’s smoke.
neboDeepWoods.name: Nebo Deep Woods

neboForestMeadow.label: Forest Meadow
neboForestMeadow.note: The pond has gone quiet. Everyone who walks this road says the same thing about that.
neboForestMeadow.intro: The pond has gone quiet. Everyone who walks this road says the same thing about that.
neboForestMeadow.name: Nebo Forest Meadow

neboForestPath.label: Forest Path
neboForestPath.note: Nine lanterns on this road. Four are dead, and not one of them is out of oil.
neboForestPath.intro: Nine lanterns on this road. Four are dead, and not one of them is out of oil.
neboForestPath.name: Nebo Path to Forest

neboGiantTreeClimb.label: The Climb
neboGiantTreeClimb.note: Eight ramps to the crown. Something has been using them ahead of you.
neboGiantTreeClimb.intro: Eight ramps to the crown. Something has been using them ahead of you.
neboGiantTreeClimb.name: Nebo Giant Tree Climb

neboGiantTreePath.label: Giant Tree Path
neboGiantTreePath.note: Warm air off the roots, where the ground should be coldest on the planet.
neboGiantTreePath.intro: Warm air off the roots, where the ground should be coldest on the planet.
neboGiantTreePath.name: Nebo Path to Giant Tree

neboGiantTreeTop.label: Tree Top
neboGiantTreeTop.note: From up here the forest is a map, and there is a ring drawn on it.
neboGiantTreeTop.intro: From up here the forest is a map, and there is a ring drawn on it.
neboGiantTreeTop.name: Nebo Giant Tree Top

neboItemShop.label: Item Shop
neboItemShop.note: Wilder has moved the lanterns to the front of the shop.
neboItemShop.name: Nebo Item Shop

neboLodge.label: Lodge
neboLodge.note: Trail counts on every wall. Two of the boards have been turned to face it.
neboLodge.name: Nebo Lodge

neboTavern.label: Tavern
neboTavern.note: Quieter than it should be at this hour. The tracker is in the corner and she is not drinking.
neboTavern.name: Nebo Tavern

neboThroneRoom.label: Throne Room
neboThroneRoom.note: Elder Nova holds Nebo lightly. He has been holding it tighter since the ridge.
neboThroneRoom.intro: Elder Nova holds Nebo lightly. He has been holding it tighter since the ridge.
neboThroneRoom.name: Nebo Throne Room

neboTownSquare.label: Nebo Town Square
neboTownSquare.note: The square is full and nobody is sitting down. Word came off the ridge before you did.
neboTownSquare.intro: The square is full and nobody is sitting down. Word came off the ridge before you did.
neboTownSquare.name: Nebo Town Square

neboHive.label: The Hive
neboHive.note: THE HIVE. The transport was interrupted here. Hold the ground and it will finish the crossing.
neboHive.intro: BATTLE. Machines and raiders are coming for the core. Hold it through three waves: fight them off, use the cover, and take out the turrets.
neboHive.name: The Hive

neboBanditFort.label: The Wick Fort
neboBanditFort.note: Stumps for four hundred paces, and a fire going in the middle of them. Somebody has been busy out here.
neboBanditFort.intro: Stumps for four hundred paces, and a fire going in the middle of them. Somebody has been busy out here.
neboBanditFort.name: The Wick Fort

neboRangerCabin.label: Ranger’s Cabin
neboRangerCabin.note: Every trail on this road, marked and counted twice. Fern says the second count is the one that ruins your week.
neboRangerCabin.name: Ranger’s Cabin

neboFarmHouse.label: Garden Farmhouse
neboFarmHouse.note: Seed, twine and a ledger of what went in where. Hazel keeps the water; this is everything else.
neboFarmHouse.name: Garden Farmhouse

neboToolShed.label: Tool Shed
neboToolShed.note: Everything with an edge on it, hung where it can be found in the dark. The shed is the tidiest building on the planet.
neboToolShed.name: Tool Shed

neboTreeHouse.label: The Tree House
neboTreeHouse.note: A platform, a bunk and a ladder you can pull up. Sorrel has been here six days.
neboTreeHouse.intro: A platform, a bunk and a ladder you can pull up. Sorrel has been here six days.
neboTreeHouse.name: The Tree House

neboLookoutHut.label: Lookout Hut
neboLookoutHut.note: Charts of the canopy, pinned and re-pinned. Kestrel measured the ring twice on this table because she did not like the answer.
neboLookoutHut.name: Lookout Hut

neboCandyShop.label: The Candy Shop
neboCandyShop.note: Warm sugar, and something on the boil. There is a card in the window that says NOW HIRING and it has been there a while.
neboCandyShop.name: The Candy Shop

neboSpacedock.label: Nebo Spacedock
neboSpacedock.note: High above Nebo. Your ship is berthed at the end of the gantry. Walk to the teleporter at the far end and it beams you down to the crest pad.
neboSpacedock.intro: High above Nebo. Your ship is berthed at the end of the gantry. Walk to the teleporter at the far end and it beams you down to the crest pad.
neboSpacedock.name: Nebo Spacedock

npcs.name: Wilder
npcs.greeting: Take a lantern. Everyone says they will not need one.
npcs.bio: Keeps the shop on the square. Half the stock is for the forest and the other half is for people who underestimated the forest.

npcs.name: Brindle
npcs.greeting: Light kit or no kit. You will be climbing before dark.
npcs.bio: Makes gear light, because everything on Nebo eventually has to be carried up something.

npcs.name: Juniper
npcs.greeting: Sit anywhere. Boots off the bench, that is the only rule.
npcs.bio: Runs the tavern and the shuffleboard league, and will tell you the league is the harder job.

npcs.name: Marlow
npcs.greeting: Mind the aviary door. Everything in there is faster than you — except the pig, and she is cleverer.
npcs.bio: Keeps the pens, the aviary and the pond. Knows every animal in here by name and half the ones outside.

stock.label: Parsnip the truffle pig, for the day

npcs.name: Rye
npcs.greeting: Seed, twine, and something for whatever is eating it.
npcs.bio: Keeps the seed store for the whole square. Has opinions about the curve in the beds and will share them.

npcs.name: Elder Nova

lines.text: Elder.
You came up the road, so you have already seen most of what we are proud of.
The tree is the rest of it. Climb it before you decide about us.

topics.label: The ridge.
replies: You held it, and I am grateful, and I am not going to pretend that was the end of it.
Nebo has been invaded twice in four hundred years. Both times, something arrived.
This time nothing arrived. Sit with that for a moment; I have been sitting with it for three weeks.

topics.label: What do you want done?
replies: Walk my forest and tell me plainly what is in it.
My wardens tell me what they believe I would like to hear. Ash does not. Start with Ash, at the lodge.

topics.label: You do not seem worried.
replies: I am extremely worried.
I am also eighty-one, and worrying loudly has never once cleared a trail.

topics.label: Elder.
replies: Go carefully. And come back and say it plainly, whatever it turns out to be.

npcs.bio: Holds Nebo, and holds it lightly. Spends more time in the garden than on the dais and does not pretend otherwise.

npcs.name: Warden Ash

lines.text: Warden.
Everything in the deep woods was fine until the glow got into it. Now some of it stands up.
Fight it in the open if you can. Under the canopy it hears you first.

topics.label: The trail counts.
replies: Eleven. Then twenty-six. Then sixty-one, and that is one road.
A thing that spreads gets bigger. A thing that goes eleven, twenty-six, sixty-one is not spreading. It is breeding.
Fern has the boards on the forest road. Ask her yourself; she will not soften it either.

topics.label: Two of your boards face the wall.
replies: Three parties out this month. Two back.
The last one was Sorrel’s, up the north spur. One of them walked out and could not finish a sentence.
Sorrel is still in there. Tree house, deep woods. I have run out of foxes to send after her, which is why I am glad to see you.

topics.label: What am I looking for?
replies: A gate that was not there yesterday. They come up out of deadfall — a stump, a fallen trunk, anything that has already stopped growing.
One standing on its own: break it.
Four of them in a ring: come back and tell me before you touch any of them. That is not a nest. That is a plan.

topics.label: I will take the road west.
replies: Take the meadow road. Not the pond side of it.

npcs.bio: Runs the lodge, the trail counts and the search parties, in that order of how often they are needed.

npcs.name: Linden

lines.text: You track the woods?
I track what walks them. Lately that includes things that did not used to walk at all.
Bramble goes where the glow goes. Find the glow and you have found tomorrow's problem.
Is the meadow safe?
In daylight, at the edges. Do not cross the middle just because it is quicker. It is not quicker.

topics.label: Read it for me.
replies: Everything new is following water. That is the whole of it and it took me a week to see.
The stream on the castle path. The river on the forest road. The pond in the meadow.
All three drain the same way — east, and down, into the root plate under the giant tree.

topics.label: So it is coming from the tree?
replies: It is coming from under everything.
The tree is only where under everything comes nearest the surface. That is why the tree is the place you can see it from, and not the place it lives.
I am a tracker, not a priest. Go up and look.

topics.label: Anything else on the road?
replies: The lanterns on the forest path keep going out.
Not blown out. Put out. There is a difference and I can show it to you in the soot.

topics.label: Thank you.
replies: Do not thank me yet. Thank me on the way back.

npcs.bio: Nebo's tracker. Reads a week-old trail the way other people read a notice board, and is unbearable about it for about a minute.

npcs.name: Kestrel

lines.text: You fly from up here?
Off the lip, out over the meadow, down at the lodge if the wind is honest. Twelve minutes on a good one.
From up here you can see the glow spreading. On the ground you only meet it.
What do you see from up here?
Everything, and it is not all good. The deep woods are darker this season than last.
Elder Nova knows. He would rather show a visitor the garden first, and honestly, so would I.

topics.label: Show me the woods.
replies: Glass is by the hut. Look south, and do not look for the gates — look for the gaps.
Every gate anyone has found sits on one line. It is not a spread. It is a RING.

topics.label: A ring around what?
replies: The town. Dead centre.
I measured it twice, because I did not care for the answer the first time.
And there is one arc of it with nothing on it yet. The south side. That is the community garden.

topics.label: How long have I got?
replies: Eleven, twenty-six, sixty-one. The last of those was counted this morning.
If you would rather be standing in the garden when it comes up than hear about it afterwards, go now.

topics.label: Going.
replies: Wind is off the north. If you fall, fall that way.

npcs.bio: Flies the canopy. Has jumped off this lip more times than anyone has counted and still checks the wind twice.

npcs.name: Bracken

lines.text: Something came down on the ridge.
We watched it from the square. Four gates, and one fox stood in the middle of them.
Warden Ash wants a word before you take the road west.

topics.label: What came down?
replies: Nothing came down. That is the part nobody will say out loud.
The gates GREW. Up out of the ridge, overnight, in a ring.
The Elder still calls it a landing. A landing is a thing that can be over.

topics.label: Where is the Warden?
replies: The lodge. North up the castle path, then east at the fork glade.
Take the road, not the verge. The verge is where the new growth is.

topics.label: Who else should I be talking to?
replies: Linden, in the tavern, if you want the trail read.
Kestrel at the crown, if you want it seen whole. She has the glass up there.
Elder Nova is in the throne room, or the garden. Usually the garden.

topics.label: I will look around.
replies: Mind the lanterns. They have been going out early.

npcs.bio: Runs the boards between the lodge and the square. Fast, and has not been asked to carry good news in three weeks.

npcs.name: Ivy

lines.text: You are the one who teaches them.
I teach them to come back. Different subject.
You have been on the ridge, so I will spare you the stance.

topics.label: What do you teach them about the new growth?
replies: That it does not tire and you do. Everything else follows from that.
Break the gate and the things it made stop arriving. Chase the things it made and you will be chasing them at nightfall.

topics.label: Two of the boards are turned to the wall.
replies: Sorrel’s party and the one before it.
Ash turns a board when she has stopped expecting the count. She has not taken them down, which is her being stubborn, and I let her.

npcs.bio: Teaches the wardens to come back, which she will tell you is a different subject from teaching them to fight.

npcs.name: Fern

lines.text: You are counting something.
New growth. I mark it, I walk back, I mark it again.
This stretch was eleven last month. It was sixty-one this morning, and I have not done the west end.

topics.label: Sixty-one.
replies: Eleven. Twenty-six. Sixty-one.
That is not something spreading. That is something breeding.
I gave the numbers to the lodge. Ash turned another board round.

topics.label: The lanterns are out.
replies: Nine on this road. Four dead, and not one of them out of oil.
Whatever puts them out does it from the top. I would like to know what is tall enough for that.

topics.label: The bridge.
replies: Cross it. Do not go down the bank.
The bank is soft now, and soft ground on this road means something has already been through it.

topics.label: I will keep going.
replies: West is the meadow. The pond has gone quiet, and that pond was never quiet.

npcs.bio: Marks new growth on the forest road, walks back, and marks it again. Has stopped enjoying the second half of that.

npcs.name: Sorrel

lines.text: Warden Ash sent me.
Then she has run out of wardens. I told her she would.
Do not stand under the trunk while we talk. Stand where you can see the trunk.

topics.label: What did you find?
replies: A gate. Sixth trunk up the north spur.
It was not there on the second pass, and the second pass was the day before.
It had grown out of the deadfall. Not landed on it — GROWN out of it, the way a bracket fungus grows out of wood that has already given up.

topics.label: What happened to your party?
replies: It opened while we were writing it down.
Two of them went down the spur. I went up the ladder.
I am the ladder. That is the whole of my report and Ash can have it in writing.

topics.label: Was there anything around it?
replies: Marks. In a ring, four of them, at the compass points.
I have seen the ridge from up here since. Same ring. Same four.
Somebody should go up the tree and look at the whole forest at once, because I have been looking at one trunk for six days and it told me nothing.

topics.label: Come down to the lodge.
replies: When the spur is clear. Not before.

npcs.bio: Six days up the north spur with a counting party of three. Came back as far as the tree house and stopped there.

npcs.name: Bryn

lines.text: You fly this?
Off the crown, down to the field. Twenty minutes up. Ninety seconds down.
It has been a bad month for it.

topics.label: Bad how?
replies: The air off the tree is wrong. Warm where it has no business being warm.
You feel it on the ramp before you feel it anywhere else on the planet.
Something under the roots is running hot, and I fly on what the air is doing, so I notice.

topics.label: Is the climb clear?
replies: It was. It is not.
There are things on the ramps that were not using the ramps last week.

topics.label: I will walk up.
replies: Kestrel is at the top. Ask her for the glass — it is worth the climb on its own.
And ask Rill for a glider on the way back down. The rings are right where you are standing.

npcs.bio: Runs the landing field. Twenty minutes up the trunk and ninety seconds down, and he will tell you which half he prefers.

npcs.name: Hazel

lines.text: How are the beds?
Dying. And before you say it: it is not the water. I do the water.
They are dying in a CURVE. That is what I want somebody to explain to me.

topics.label: A curve.
replies: West bed to east bed, bowed, and widening every week.
If you stand on the north gate and sight along it, it bears on the amphitheatre.
Whatever is doing it is aiming at the middle of my garden.

topics.label: You should get everyone out.
replies: Everyone is out.
I stayed to lock the shed, which I am aware is the stupidest sentence I have said this year.

topics.label: They are doing the play?
replies: Over my beds, with a run under them the size of my arm. Yes they are.
Marigold says the play goes on whatever is under the ground.
I have started to think she is right, which is what frightens me.

topics.label: If something comes up here, stand back.
replies: Behind the toolshed, and I will not argue.
Break them and I will replant by spring. I have done it after a fire; I can do it after this.

npcs.bio: Keeps the beds, the water and the amphitheatre. Will correct you about the water, at length, and will be right.

npcs.name: Marten

lines.text: These are all counts?
Every one. Fern marks them, I copy them up, and we both check the total.
We have started checking it twice. That is not a good sign about a total.

topics.label: What do the boards say?
replies: Eleven, twenty-six, sixty-one. Left to right, three weeks.
And the fourth board is up but not filled in, because Fern has not finished the west end.
I have a guess about the fourth board and I would rather be wrong.

topics.label: Why two counts?
replies: Because the first time we thought we had miscounted.
You do not check a number twice when you like it.

topics.label: I will let you get on.
replies: Shut the door. Whatever is out there, I would rather it stayed out there.

npcs.bio: Walks the road when Fern does not, which lately is never. Keeps the boards up to date and does not enjoy it.

npcs.name: Angelica

lines.text: Any chance you are looking for a job? We got great candies here, super fun to make.

topics.label: How do I make candy?
replies: Sugar and heat, and the heat is the whole of it. Soft ball is chewy, firm ball springs, hard crack goes like glass.
Boil it to the band the sweet wants, call it off, then it is your hands: pull it, pipe it, roll it or temper it.

topics.label: How did you get into the candy business?
replies: My mother kept bees at the top of the ridge and I kept eating the honey, so she gave me a pan and told me to make my own trouble.
Thirty years of it. I still cannot walk past a rolling boil without putting a finger in the water.

topics.label: I will come back.
replies: Door is open. It smells better in here than out there.

npcs.bio: Runs the coppers and the counter. Has been one pair of hands short since the spring and says so to everyone who comes in.

npcs.name: Rill

lines.text: YOU cleared the PATH! That earns you a flight for FREE!

topics.label: How does it work?
replies: Lean it and it turns. Height is all you have — turning spends it and so does slowing down.
Circle the warm columns to get some back. Three rings on the field, and landing slow pays a quarter more.

topics.label: Why did the bees become angry and how did the QUEEN get SOOO big!?
replies: It seems that animals are becoming aggressive all over the galaxy.
The Keepers of the TREES say that NEBO is calling out for help, but they don't know help with what.

npcs.bio: Runs the lip and the book on it. Has watched more landings than anyone on Nebo and will describe every one of them.

npcs.name: Marigold

lines.text: You are early. Or you are late — we have been at this since the frost.
Four moves and a drum. Sun, rain, earth, wind. That is the whole play.
And the thanks?
The thanks is the reason. The dance is only how we say it.

topics.label: Who are you thanking?
replies: Whoever set the first seed. We do not claim to know the name.
It came up green without being asked to and it has done it every year since.
You can call that luck if you like. We call it worth an afternoon.

topics.label: What is the play about?
replies: A year. Sun, then rain, then what the earth does about it, then the wind that takes it away.
It is four moves long because a year is four moves long.
Anyone who says it is longer than that has never grown anything.

topics.label: I will come back.
replies: The boards will be here. So will we.

npcs.bio: Calls the harvest play, and has called it for nineteen years. Writes the invocation fresh every year and it comes out the same.

npcs.name: Bramble

lines.text: I am the sun. I come up. That is the part.

topics.label: Is it hard?
replies: Coming up is easy. Going down slowly is the hard half.

topics.label: Good luck.
replies: We do not need luck. We need rain.

npcs.bio: Dances the sun. Has done since he was small enough to be carried on.

npcs.name: Thistle

lines.text: Eleven years I have been the rain and it has worked four times.

topics.label: Four out of eleven?
replies: Which is four more than nothing, and nobody else is trying.

topics.label: Good luck.
replies: Watch my feet, not the sky.

npcs.bio: Dances the rain, eleven years running, and still counts under his breath.

npcs.name: Quill

lines.text: Earth does not move much. Try it for a whole verse.

topics.label: What is under the beds?
replies: Something with claws on it. Hazel found a run last week and stopped looking.
We are doing the play anyway. That is rather the point of a play.

topics.label: Good luck.
replies: Stand where I stand and you will be fine.

npcs.bio: Dances the earth, which is the part that stays still and is hardest.

npcs.name: Pippin

lines.text: I am the wind! I get to knock everything over at the end!

topics.label: Show me the wind.
replies: You have to go all the way round. TWICE.
Marigold says once. Marigold is wrong.

topics.label: Good luck.
replies: You too! Do not stand near me!

npcs.bio: Dances the wind. Is nine. Is better at it than anyone.

npcs.name: Rooke

lines.text: You are not one of theirs. That is the first good thing to happen up here.
Rooke?
Eight days. Ask what you came to ask; I am not going anywhere.

topics.label: Eight days on a stump.
replies: Nine lanterns on this road. Four out. I came up to write down which four and when.
I got as far as writing down which four.

topics.label: Sit tight.
replies: I have had a great deal of practice.

npcs.bio: Keeps the lantern count for the forest road. Walked the west track to find out why four of them had stopped, and the people who stopped them put him in a cage.

npcs.name: Alder

lines.text: You are the one with the list.
I am the one with the list. It is not long. That is not the comfort people think it is.
Nova does the deciding. I do the writing down, and the writing down is how anybody knows anything.

topics.label: Who writes on it?
replies: Wardens, mostly. Ash sends up what Fern sends down, and I copy it out fair.
A thing gets on the list when two foxes say it and one of them is sober.

topics.label: I will come back.
replies: It will still be here. That is rather the trouble with a list.

npcs.bio: Keeps the Elder’s list of what is outstanding on Nebo. Has never once been asked to keep a list of what is going well.

npcs.name: Barley

lines.text: Busy?
Emptier than a Thursday has any business being, and I know exactly why.
Nobody wants to walk home east past that tree.

topics.label: Who drinks in here?
replies: Wardens, glider crew, and one fox who climbs the tree for a living and will not say why.
And Linden, who reads. Ask her about water; do not ask me.

topics.label: Just passing through.
replies: Everybody says that, and then everybody sits down.

npcs.bio: Runs the tavern, hears everything twice, and has closed at nine like a bakery since the frost.

npcs.name: Nettle

lines.text: You keep animals.
I keep animals. Three foxes have brought me a mole this month and not one of them brought me a mole.
I know what a mole is. I have four. They are asleep in that box and they are lovely.

topics.label: What were they, then?
replies: Bigger. And the hands are wrong. A mole digs with a spade; whatever these are dig with knives.
And a mole eats worms. The thing in the allotment is eating the CROP, and no mole has ever done that in the history of moles.

topics.label: What is the pig for?
replies: Parsnip? Truffles. She has a nose on her that would find one through a wall, and she will not be told where to look because she is already right.
Marlow rents her by the day. Walk her where the trees are and do not help — helping is how people lose an afternoon.
Angelica in the candy shop takes eight off you for a box of mints. The rest she buys, and she pays properly.

topics.label: Where do I look?
replies: South of the square, through the gates, the community garden.
Ask for Hazel. Do not say the word mole to her; she has had a month of it.

npcs.bio: Keeps the pet store, and four moles, which is four more moles than anybody else in this town has ever met.

npcs.name: Sedge

lines.text: You are in a hurry.
South. Past the gates. They are doing the harvest play and I have not missed one in nine years.
Four moves and a drum. You could learn it in an afternoon and it takes them from the frost.

topics.label: What is it for?
replies: The year. Sun, then rain, then what the earth does about it, then the wind that takes it away.
And the thanks, which is the whole reason for the other four.

topics.label: Enjoy it.
replies: Come down. Stand near the boards and Marigold will put you in it.

npcs.bio: Has not missed a harvest play in nine years and is not about to start by standing in the square talking to a stranger.

npcs.name: Hob

lines.text: You sharpen.
I sharpen. Everything on this planet that cuts has been across that stone, most of it twice.
Do not put a warden’s axe down on my counter blade first. I will see it, and I will say something.

topics.label: What comes in most?
replies: Billhooks in autumn. Saws in a wet spring.
Everything blunt has a reason and the reason is nearly always the ground it went into.

topics.label: Can you fix anything?
replies: Anything with an edge. Nothing with a spring.
Take a spring to Brindle, and do not tell her I sent you, because she will make it about springs.

npcs.bio: Sharpens for the whole town and remembers every blade he has ever had across the stone, which he will tell you about.

npcs.name: Larkin

lines.text: What is the book?
Every card flown off that crown since my grandmother ruled the first page. If you have landed, you are in it.
I do not fly. I write. One of those is a skill and the other is a hobby, and I will not be told which is which.

topics.label: Why up here?
replies: Because you can see the crown of the tree and the lip they go off, and I need to see the lip.
A card is three runs and a landing. If I only had the landing I would be writing down rumours, and there is enough of that in the tavern.

topics.label: Has anybody been hurt?
replies: Not off the lip. Twice off the ramps, both of them walking.
Write that down somewhere a flier can see it and they stop listening. Write it in a book and they read it on a wet day.

npcs.bio: Keeps the landing book for the giant tree, and has never once been up it.

npcs.name: Fallow

lines.text: You are a warden?
I have the green and I have the strap and I have not been past the picket once.
Ash will not send anybody else up the spur until somebody comes back down it, and nobody has come back down it.

topics.label: What is the strap for?
replies: A count book. Sorrel has hers, Fern has hers, and mine is empty because I have counted nothing.
Marten says an empty book is still a book. Marten has a desk.

npcs.bio: Ash’s next warden up the north spur, sitting in a cabin because there is no north spur to be sent up.

npcs.name: Holt

lines.text: Do I need to be let in?
You need to be seen coming. That is not the same thing and it is the whole of my job.
Eleven years on this arch. It has never once been shut and I would not know how.

topics.label: What is up there?
replies: The hall, the dais, and the Elder, in that order and never in any other one.
The lodge is off the fork, east. If you want a warden rather than a ruler, go right.

topics.label: Quiet post?
replies: It was. We used to count carts.
Now we count foxes coming down off the forest road with their ears flat, and I would rather have the carts.

npcs.bio: Stands the castle arch and has done for eleven years. Has never shut the gate and does not intend to be the first.

npcs.name: Vetch

lines.text: You have not said anything.
I have written you down.
Holt talks to them. I keep the tally. Between us the arch is covered.

topics.label: What are you counting?
replies: Up, and down. Everybody, both ways, since the frost.
The numbers have not gone up. They have stopped matching, which is worse and much harder to say out loud.

npcs.bio: Keeps the tally at the castle arch. Says roughly one word for every nine of Holt’s and means all of them.

npcs.name: Teasel

lines.text: The road goes straight across.
The road does. I do not.
Two months I have gone round the edge of this meadow and I have got the calves for it now, which is the only good thing I can tell you about the arrangement.

topics.label: What is out there?
replies: Lights, in the reeds, that are not on the water.
And something in the long grass on the north side that moves when I stop, which is the wrong way round.

topics.label: Does anybody go across?
replies: Foxes in a hurry. Once.
I am not saying anything happened to them. I am saying I have not asked.

npcs.bio: Goes round the edge of the meadow rather than across it, four times the distance, every day since the frost.

npcs.name: Shrike the Snuffer

lines.text: A new face at the fire... Are you here to join us?
Sit down before you answer. Nobody has ever answered that standing up and meant it.

npcs.bio: Carries a lamplighter’s pole and uses it the wrong way round. Has somebody else’s ledger under her arm and has never opened it.

npcs.name: Faller

lines.text: Mind where you put your feet. Half of what you are standing on was standing up last month.

topics.label: How many have you taken?
replies: Four hundred paces of them. I stopped counting at the ridge because counting is Tally’s job and I got bored of being right.
They do not feel it. That is the part town foxes cannot get past.

topics.label: And then what?
replies: Then the next four hundred. There is no then. There is only more of it, and that is what makes it restful.

npcs.bio: Believes the wood is stock. Cuts in the morning, burns in the afternoon, and has not been asked a hard question in a year.

npcs.name: Stoker

lines.text: Sit closer. It is a good fire and there is a great deal more where it came from.

topics.label: What are you burning?
replies: Whatever Faller brings down. Green wood spits, so we stack it a week, and a week is nothing when the stack is a wood.
Everything that burns is a thing that was waiting to be useful.

topics.label: Does it ever go out?
replies: Not since the roof went on. Shrike says a fire that goes out is an argument you have lost.

npcs.bio: Believes the wood is stock. Cuts in the morning, burns in the afternoon, and has not been asked a hard question in a year.

npcs.name: Hauler

lines.text: You will want to stand back when the sledge comes past. It does not steer.

topics.label: Where does it all go?
replies: Down the east track and onto the forge. Timber in, charcoal out, charcoal in, edges out.
We are not making furniture. Nobody here has ever made a chair.

topics.label: Edges for what?
replies: For taking more. An axe is the only tool that pays for itself in its own material.

npcs.bio: Believes the wood is stock. Cuts in the morning, burns in the afternoon, and has not been asked a hard question in a year.

npcs.name: Bellows

lines.text: Two hundred a minute on the long bag. I can talk and do it, so ask.

topics.label: You are a smith?
replies: I am the wind. The smith is the one with the burns.
Heads, mostly. Heads and points. There is no call for pots.

topics.label: Who is all this for?
replies: Society. Shrike’s word. It means whoever is holding the axe, and it is a very restful word once you stop poking it.

npcs.bio: Believes the wood is stock. Cuts in the morning, burns in the afternoon, and has not been asked a hard question in a year.

npcs.name: Tally

lines.text: Do not tell me your name. I write down what comes in and what goes out and you are not either yet.

topics.label: You keep the book?
replies: I keep four. Stems, cords, heads, and the one nobody asks about.
There is a ledger in the throne room I did not write and am not allowed to open. Ask her about it and watch her face do nothing.

topics.label: What does the wood get?
replies: A line in a book. That is more than it had.

npcs.bio: Believes the wood is stock. Cuts in the morning, burns in the afternoon, and has not been asked a hard question in a year.

npcs.name: Wick

lines.text: You came up the east track in the dark. Brave, or you have not heard.

topics.label: Why is the road unlit?
replies: Because a lantern is a tree burning for nobody. Four of them on that road, burning all night, warming the air.
We put them out and took the oil. Shrike did the last one herself. That is where the name comes from.

topics.label: People walk that road.
replies: People can carry their own light. It is not the wood’s job to see them home.

npcs.bio: Believes the wood is stock. Cuts in the morning, burns in the afternoon, and has not been asked a hard question in a year.

npcs.name: Rowan

lines.text: Quiet here.
It is the trees. They take the noise out of everything.

npcs.bio: Lights the square's lanterns and swears the mushrooms do a better job.

npcs.name: Pica

lines.text: What is east?
Forest road, then the meadow. Keep going and you reach the deep woods, which I would not.

npcs.bio: Walks the forest road daily and has never once been lost on it.

npcs.name: Tarn

lines.text: That tree.
You can climb it. People do. The view is worth the legs.

npcs.bio: Grows the prize marrows. Will bring them up unprompted.

npcs.name: Aspen

lines.text: Hello.
Evening. It is always about to be evening under this canopy.

npcs.bio: Climbed the tree at nine and has been telling people about it since.

npcs.name: Wren

lines.text: Who runs Nebo?
The castle up the north road. The lodge does the actual work.

npcs.bio: Keeps the bird count for the lodge. It is going up.

npcs.name: Fable

lines.text: Anything to see?
The garden, south. Somebody grows prize marrows and takes it very seriously.

npcs.bio: Runs the shuffleboard league at the tavern with an iron hand.

npcs.name: Pell

lines.text: Long road.
Up it and down it. I am not a warden — I carry the post.
Castle at the top, lodge off the fork. Everything anybody writes on this planet goes past my feet twice.

npcs.bio: Walks the castle road with the post, twice a day, and has an opinion about every gate on it.

lines.text: Welcome to Nebo, Steward.
Your ship is fuelled and berthed behind you. The teleporter at the end of the gantry puts you down on the crest pad in town.

topics.label: How do I get back to space?
replies: Walk back to your ship and board her. She will take you up to orbit.
